summary: This bill requires the Comptroller General to hire an independent auditor to perform a full physical assay, inventory, and audit of all U.S. gold reserves (including deep storage and any gold held by third parties) within nine months, repeat the process every five years, account for all encumbrances and transactions over the past 50 years, assess security measures, and publicly release the results with minimal redactions.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates an audit and inventory of gold reserves by the Comptroller General using an external auditor. While this entails some administrative costs, the legislation does not authorize, expand, or reduce any government spending programs or appropriations. It is strictly an oversight and transparency measure with no bearing on spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any changes to the tax code. It focuses exclusively on auditing physical gold holdings.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare policy, insurance, public coverage, or market-based healthcare systems.
The bill has no connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration, border policy, visas, or related protections or restrictions.
The legislation does not engage with reproductive rights, abortion access, or any related regulations.
While gold reserves have historical ties to monetary systems that can indirectly support defense financing, the bill itself only requires audits and does not alter military or defense spending.
No environmental regulations, climate policies, or conservation measures are addressed.
The bill does not modify welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net expenditures.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, school choice, or federal involvement in education.
The bill contains nothing about drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No criminal justice reforms, sentencing changes, or policing measures are included.
Although gold can feature in international finance, the bill is limited to domestic auditing and transparency requirements and does not alter trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization policies.

Gold reserves represent a national asset that could theoretically relate to balance-sheet considerations, but the bill only mandates periodic audits and public reporting. It neither promotes deficit spending nor prioritizes debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
The bill does not modify, expand, or reduce foreign aid programs.
No election integrity, voting access, or electoral reform measures are present.
The legislation does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No labor, union, or workplace policy provisions are included.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions, civil rights priorities, or anti-discrimination rules.
